title: Making it up
hookLine: missed days are made up later, or a poor person fed for each day if unable

cards: It's Sha'ban, the month before Ramadan, and in a house in Medina a woman is keeping fasts that belong to last Ramadan. She isn't adding anything extra. She's paying back.
The woman is Aisha, wife of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and she says it herself in Sahih al-Bukhari: she would have days of Ramadan to make up, and she couldn't make them up until Sha'ban.
Months could pass with that small debt waiting. Today's word is the name for paying it.

teach.b: The word is qada': making up an act of worship after its time has passed. First, it comes straight from yesterday's verse. The sick and the traveler fast, in Pickthall's words, "(the same) number of other days."
The next verse gives a reason: Allah desires ease, and desires "that ye should complete the period." So the allowance doesn't erase the days. It moves them.
Second, Aisha shows the timing can be loose. She made up her days in Sha'ban, just before the next Ramadan.
Scholars take from this that make-up days can wait, though not past the next Ramadan; schools differ on what's owed if someone lets them slide past that without a reason.

teach.h: THE DAYS MOVE, THEY DON'T VANISH.
teach.b: Third, the days don't have to be in a row. The verse says only other days, and scholars read that as allowing them to be spread out: a Monday here, a Thursday there, a quiet Saturday in winter when the days are short.
Yesterday's report from Aisha in Sahih Muslim fits here too: women make up the fasts missed during their periods.

Fourth, one more case, and tomorrow is about it. Some people will never be able to make the days up: the very old, the permanently ill. For them the verse has another answer, and it involves feeding someone.

teach.h: THAT YE SHOULD COMPLETE THE PERIOD.
teach.b: Away from the fast, qada' is a way of thinking about any commitment you couldn't keep on time. Not canceled. Not a failure.
Owed, and waiting for its day.

how: Muslims who miss Ramadan fasts for illness, travel, pregnancy, nursing or menstruation fast the same number of days later in the year, before the next Ramadan, together or spread out.

o: fasting extra days to earn more reward than others
fasting missed Ramadan days later, on other days

games.q: you missed days of Ramadan while ill. it's months later, and the next Ramadan is coming. what does Aisha's report show?
o: the days are lost once Ramadan ends.
they can wait, and she made hers up in Sha'ban.
they must be fasted the week after Ramadan.
games.why: Aisha made hers up in Sha'ban, the month before the next Ramadan. the make-up can wait, but the days are still owed.

practice: If you fast and owe days, see a calendar in your mind and quietly place them, which weeks, which days, before the next Ramadan.

If you don't, find one thing you meant to do and didn't, a call you owe, a thank-you note, a visit you postponed, and without scolding yourself, give it a date. If you pray, you can ask Allah to make it easy.

wordCard.voice: Qada'. Making up a missed act of worship after its time; here, fasting the missed days of Ramadan later in the year. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: in law, making up worship after its time.

carryVoice: Your line: made up later. The days are moved, never simply erased. See you tomorrow.
